title: How Much Water Is on Earth, Really?
lines: How much water is there on Earth, really?
Oceans cover {71 percent~seventy-one percent} of the planet.
Now gather every drop: | the oceans, the ice caps, the lakes, the rivers, even the clouds.
Pull it all together into one ball.
It would be just {1,385~one thousand three hundred eighty-five} kilometers across.
That's less than half the width of the Moon.
Next to Earth, it's a small blue bead.
Now keep only the liquid fresh water: | the lakes, the rivers, the swamps, the groundwater.
That ball is just {273~two hundred seventy-three} kilometers wide.
And the fresh water in every lake and river on the planet?
A tiny drop, about {56~fifty-six} kilometers across. | Roughly the width of London.
That's what so much of life depends on.
A blue planet, | with surprisingly little water.
Did you think there was more water? | Way more, about this, or less? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: All of Earth's water | would fit in a ball smaller than the Moon.
